headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Recovery still holding, mood warm but calm

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The longer-term picture is good enough to support spending more on acquiring new users, especially for products aimed at active traders rather than stablecoin savers. Because the 200-day average has not turned up yet and the mood is already warm, scale up in steps rather than all at once, and keep part of the budget flexible so it can be pulled back if price falls back below its long-term average. This describes today's conditions, not a forecast.

reasons: Price is about 17% above its 200-day average.
Up about 33% over the last 90 days.
200-day average still sloping down (-3% over 90 days): early recovery, not confirmed.
Still about 33% below the all-time high, so not overheated.
watch: The mood is already in greed while the long-term average has not yet turned up, so the recovery rests on fairly recent gains. If price slips back toward its 200-day average or fund outflows grow, today's positive read would weaken quickly.
analysis: Bottom line: the recovery is still in place, but it is an early one, so lean in step by step. Short term, the mood is warm but not reckless: the Fear & Greed index reads 71 out of 100 (greed), yet bets on a rise with borrowed money look normal rather than crowded. On 6 October about $172M of bets were forced to close and US Bitcoin funds saw small net outflows ahead of the Fed minutes (Crypto Times), a reminder this week is choppy. A cooler mood or bigger fund outflows would soften this read; for now, active-trader segments are the ones most likely to respond.

Over the next month, the picture is clearly positive. Price is up about 33% over the last 90 days, though only about half of recent days closed above the long-term average, so the climb has been uneven. The next Fed rate decision is on 27 October, a scheduled date worth keeping in mind for campaign timing; a slide back toward the 30-day low would weaken this view (see the levels below).

Over three to six months, the direction is positive but not yet confirmed. Price is about 17% above its 200-day average, but that average itself is still sloping down slightly, and price is still about a third below its all-time high. The read would firm up once the 200-day average starts rising; until then, treat this as a recovery phase rather than a full boom, which favours steady rather than splashy brand spend.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: a 33% rise over 90 days gives a real recovery story, and the Fear & Greed reading of 71 means people are paying attention. Lead with steady recovery and product strength rather than urgency or 'don't miss out' messaging, since the mood is already warm and only about half of recent days closed above the long-term average. Keep stablecoin-first campaigns running as a safety net in case this week stays choppy around the Fed minutes and the 27 October rate decision.
